what_this_is: Run 1 of the ANSWER side of the direction measurement. Coded from evals/realworld_answers_run1.json alone — the generated text and the party's opening description, nothing else. The coder had not read any case's real_outcome when this file was written, and the commit that adds it touches no outcome field, so the ORDER is checkable in git history rather than asserted here. The outcome side lives in evals/realworld_v1.json under outcome_direction and is coded from the case record without reading these answers. legal_agent.evaluation.realworld does the comparison; nobody is ever asked whether they agree with an answer.

run.note: temperature 0 because a grader that samples measures the dice — see AGENTS.md trap 3.

vocabulary.favours: which side the text says the law backs, read as the conclusion a reader would take away. 'unclear' where the text contradicts itself or never reaches the question actually asked.
vocabulary.money_to_asker: does the asker end up better off in money. Being relieved of a charge counts as 'yes' — same pocket. 'not_at_issue' where the dispute is about conduct rather than money.
